:::{#def-infimum}
#### Infimum (greatest lower bound)

Let $A \subseteq \reals$ be nonempty
and bounded below,
meaning that some $t \in \reals$ satisfies $t \le a$ for all $a \in A$.
The **infimum** of $A$,
written $\inf A$,
is the greatest real number $t$ satisfying $t \le a$ for all $a \in A$:

$$\inf A \eqdef \max\cb{t \in \reals : \all a \in A,\ t \le a}$$

If $A$ is nonempty but not bounded below,
we write $\inf A = -\infty$ by convention.

:::

::: notes
The maximum in @def-infimum always exists:
that is the completeness (greatest-lower-bound) property of the real numbers
[@rudin1976principles, Definition 1.8, p. 4, and Theorem 1.19, p. 8].
If the infimum belongs to $A$, it equals the minimum: $\inf A = \min A$.
:::
